title: Other cornet players: Manuel Mello, Lawrence Vega and a friend
summary: Allen asks about early cornetists; Brunies says Mello was Laine's son-in-law, Vega was older and hot, and recalls a friend who sat in at dances.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: I was going to ask about some of the other old-time cornet players that maybe you worked with or got to hear, like Manuel Mello.
Manuel, yeah. That's Lane's son-in-law. Old man Lane.
No, about the same age. About the same age. He's a lion. Works on the poles. He used to do it. He used to play trumpet, too.

And Lawrence Vega. Lawrence Vega. Is he older than you or about the same age? Oh, he's older. Older man than you. He's dead, too. He was hot, too. Is he a good hot trumpet player that played ragtime? Oh, yeah.
How about your friend on Constant Street, the Italian man that was... Oh, yeah.
Oh, yeah. How did he play in the old days?

He was an uncle. Really? To me, he was in my time. We used to play up at Beznor's. Had a band up at Beznor's. And before he had to do a trumpet. We used to play up at Olderwise, dancing school. Olderwise. And he used to come up there. And when I was going to take intermission, go out and sit down in my chair and take my trumpet and pull with it like that. All of a sudden, he was like, I don't know how to play it. He did good, too. Oh, yeah. I see. He fusses. He said he writes articles and I think he misses all of all the jazz.
